rationale: C03 is the closest because both directives extend an expiring legal period, but its trademark-renewal proclamation uses a distinct statutory findings framework and does not share the child's concrete formulation, exception, or operative machinery. The resemblance is only the generic act of extending a deadline. C01 concerns delegated economic-control authority and procedures, while C02 implements a Cuban trade agreement through tariff modifications; neither plausibly supplied material drafting for the extension of Indian-land trust restrictions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: which, unless extended, will expire during the calendar year 1948 ... extended for a further period of twenty-five years
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the time within which compliance with conditions and formalities prescribed with respect to renewal ... is hereby extended ... until and including June 30, 1948
shared_material.explanation: Both use an extension to prevent or address expiration, but this is generic legal-administrative language applied through materially different structures and is insufficient to establish a reusable drafting template.
